age.evidence: Mice were 8-12 weeks old at the time of experiments

sex.evidence: All experiments were carried out on male C57BL/6JRj mice

handling.evidence: Before the first behavioral test, mice were habituated to handling by the male experimenter for approximately two minutes per day on three consecutive days.

assays.assay_description: Mice were placed in a single-housing cage (268 × 215 × 141 mm) with fresh bedding mixed with home-cage bedding, habituated for 60 min, then injected with vehicle or DOI (0.2 or 2.0 mg/kg i.p.). Behavior was video-recorded for 15 min; head twitches were scored manually by a blinded observer and distance traveled was extracted with Ethovision XT.

application_type.evidence: DOI was diluted to the final concentration in an intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection volume of 10 mL/kg.

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were placed in a single housing cage ... in the experimental room for a habituation period of 60 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in a single housing cage ... and their behavior was recorded

food_restriction.evidence: Testing in single housing cage with bedding only; food not mentioned as present in the testing cage

water_restriction.evidence: Testing in single housing cage with bedding only; water not mentioned as present in the testing cage

time_to_assay.evidence: Behavior of mice was immediately recorded for locomotor activity and head twitch assessment.

sample_size.evidence: vehicle solution (1% DMSO in saline, Con: n = 16, Str: n = 12) or DOI (low dose: 0.2 mg/kg, Con: n = 16, Str: n = 10; high dose: 2.0 mg/kg, Con: n = 16, Str: n = 10)

outcomes.summary: DOI dose-dependently increased head twitch responses, and this effect was not influenced by prior swim-stress exposure. DOI had no significant effect on distance traveled.
outcomes.evidence: DOI dose-dependently increased head twitch responses but the effect of DOI was not influenced by prior stress exposure (Figure 1B; treatment: F(1, 48) = 152.9, p < 0.0001).

assays.assay_description: Mice were placed in a brightly illuminated glass cylinder (16 cm diameter, 24 cm height) filled with water (25 ± 1 °C, 17 cm deep) for 5 min on day 7 (24 h after DOI). A blinded observer classified the predominant behavior (immobility, swimming, climbing) per 5 s interval; latency to immobility was also recorded. A 15 min pre-exposure to swim stress on day 0 served as the stress manipulation.

application_type.evidence: DOI was diluted to the final concentration in an intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection volume of 10 mL/kg

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation to the swim apparatus is described prior to the 5-min test; the day-0 swim exposure is the stress manipulation, not apparatus habituation

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in a... cylinder glass tank... filled with tap water (25 ± 1 °C, 17 cm deep). FST cylinders are categorized as restraint per rubric.

food_restriction.evidence: FST cylinder with water only; no food accessible during testing

water_restriction.evidence: FST cylinder; no drinking water accessible during testing

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice received a single administration of DOI on day 6. The forced swim test was performed on day 7

sample_size.evidence: vehicle (Con: n = 16, Str: n = 12) or DOI (low dose: Con n = 16, Str n = 10; high dose: Con n = 16, Str n = 10); ANOVA df F(2,74) consistent with ~80 mice

outcomes.summary: Prior swim stress reduced latency to immobility, eliminated climbing, and increased immobility. DOI treatment had a significant effect on immobility (F(2,74)=3.19, p=0.047): the low dose (0.2 mg/kg) significantly increased immobility in stress-exposed mice (p=0.01), while the high dose (2 mg/kg) had no significant effect. DOI did not significantly affect latency to immobility, climbing, or swimming.
outcomes.statistics: Latency: treatment F(2,74)=0.24, p=0.79; stress F(1,74)=85.75, p<0.0001; interaction F(2,74)=0.52, p=0.60. Immobility: treatment F(2,74)=3.19, p=0.047; stress F(1,74)=22.94, p<0.0001; interaction F(2,74)=2.70, p=0.07; post-hoc low dose vs vehicle in stressed mice p=0.01. Climbing: treatment F(2,74)=1.97, p=0.15; stress F(1,74)=64.91, p<0.0001. Swimming: treatment F(2,74)=2.62, p=0.08.
outcomes.evidence: Post-hoc analysis revealed that the lowest dose of DOI significantly increased immobility in mice previously exposed to swim stress (p = 0.01).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency to immobility, immobility count, climbing behavior, swimming behavior (4 measures)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: The analysis was performed on the counts of predominant behaviors (totals over the 5 min test)

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: no analysis of transitions or behavioural sequences reported

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility/swimming/climbing are not ethological per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: An observer that was blinded to treatment analyzed the stress-coping behavior ... by classifying the most predominant behavior per 5 sec interval.

E1_environment_type.evidence: cylinder glass tank (diameter: 16 cm, height: 24 cm) filled with tap water

E2_shelter.evidence: definitionally absent - FST cylinder has no refuge

E3_bedding.evidence: filled with tap water - no bedding

E8_food_water.evidence: definitionally absent - no food/drinking water in FST

D1_continuity.evidence: subjected to a 5 min forced swim test on day 7 (data analyzed from this single test; day-0 swim was stress manipulation only)

D2_session_duration.evidence: subjected to a 5 min forced swim test

D3_recording_days.evidence: FST behaviour analyzed on a single day (day 7); the day-0 15 min swim exposure was a stress manipulation, not analyzed as FST data here

D5_followup.evidence: DOI administered on day 6, FST performed on day 7 (~24 h post-dose)

D6_circadian.evidence: 5 min session does not span >=6 hours

judge_notes: Merged candidate gptoss's separate 'Head Twitch Response' and 'Locomotor Activity' assays into one entry because they were recorded simultaneously from the same 15-min video in the same testing cage; B1 captures both head-twitch and locomotion as distinct measures (score 2-3).
B1 for HTR assay set to 1 (2-3 measures) because both head-twitch count and locomotor distance were reported, consistent with qwen.
FST B1 set to 2 (4-6) reflecting latency, immobility, climbing, swimming (4 measures).

FST direction set to 'mixed': overall treatment ANOVA was significant (p=0.047) with low dose INCREASING immobility in stressed mice (opposite of antidepressant-like decrease), while other measures (latency, climbing, swimming) showed no significant DOI effect — does not fit a single clean direction.
Vehicle classified as DMSO (primary solvent of working solution: '5% V/V DMSO in sterile saline'); evidence mentions saline as diluent.
FST D3 = 1: the 15-min day-0 swim was the stress manipulation (not analyzed as an FST behavioural outcome in the paper); only the day-7 5-min test is the FST recording day.
FST setup_restrain = yes per rubric (FST cylinders explicitly listed as restraint).
